questions.prompt: Which wall was built across northern Britain by order of an emperor in AD 122?
questions.fact: A later emperor built a second wall further north, held it for about twenty years, then abandoned it and fell back to this one.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
questions.fact: It comes from kalium, the Latin name, which is itself borrowed from an Arabic word for plant ash.

questions.prompt: In which sport is the Stanley Cup awarded?
questions.fact: Every player on the winning team traditionally gets it for a day, and it has been used as a cereal bowl and a dog dish.

questions.prompt: Which film features a hotel called the Overlook?
questions.fact: Its author disliked the adaptation enough to fund a second, more faithful version for television twenty years later.

questions.prompt: Which country has the most natural lakes?
questions.fact: It holds more lake area than the rest of the world combined, nearly all of it carved by retreating ice sheets.

questions.prompt: Which novel features a boy stranded at sea with a tiger?
options: The Old Man and the Sea
questions.fact: It was rejected by several London publishers before winning the Booker Prize.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym RAM's opposite storage type ROM stand for?
questions.fact: Its contents are written once at manufacture, which is why the earliest game cartridges could not be saved to.
